text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were slightly higher, buffeted throughout the day by Treasuries and worries about the direction of U.S. interest rates. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.48, up 0.06 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts pared gains late in the session and closed only 1/32 up on the day, having traded as much as 10/32 higher. Dealers said the market's performance was disappointing given the soft U.S. prices data and Treasuries' smart bounce. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-05/32, up 01/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled just marginally in the red after market-positive U.S. producer price data in the afternoon buoyed the U.S. market and pulled French debt out of its early morning retreat. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.30, down 0.16 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures closed weaker but off session lows after fluctuating in a fairly narrow late trading range with doubts about domestic budget measures and EMU continuing to weigh on sentiment. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.68, down 0.29 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries remain a bit higher in mid-morning trade with the market expected to range-trade for rest of day with activity light. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-26/32, up 10/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.95 percent.

JAPAN - The yield of the benchmark three percent 182nd 10-year JGB hit a record low of 2.190 percent in late Tokyo trading on aggressive investor buying and a talk of the postponement of the 10-year JGB auction. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.58, up 0.30 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market business slowed, ahead of the weekend and amid uncertainty in the U.S. Treasury market. PUMA, Australia's largest private sector mortgage-backed bond issuer, said in Sydney it will launch a three-tranche FRN totalling $700 million next Monday. The deal, to be lead managed by J.P. Morgan, has been in the offing for over the year with all involved waiting for a change in Australian withholding tax law before launching the issue.
